method: Pairwise cosine over 24 existing images with 2 recognisers (OpenCV SFace, ArcFace w600k_r50) on the same SFace-aligned 112x112 crop. The positive set is within-character pairs among the reference-bound ch-jun and ch-rio close-up sets, where portraits 02-05 were generated from portrait 01 as the reference and accepted as that character. The negative set is every cross-character pair among ch-lia, ch-jun and ch-rio. No operator labelling was available; these are the strongest same/different labels the repository already carries.
separation: The two distributions do not overlap and nothing lands between 0.551 and 0.831. OpenCV's documented 0.363 same-identity line for SFace sits inside the negative distribution here and must not be used on this material.

bands.same: at or above the positive floor - identity held to the standard reference-bound generation already demonstrates
bands.drift: between the negative ceiling and the positive floor - not a different person by the recogniser, not the same one either; this is where the beauty-prior collapse lives and where the operator's eye rejects the image
bands.different: at or below the negative ceiling - a different person

uncalibrated_buckets.deep_three_quarter: No same-identity pair at this yaw exists yet. A recogniser trained on real photographs loses accuracy off-axis, so the frontal line would reject correct frames. Calibrate from within-clip pairs of a turnaround, which are the same person by construction.
uncalibrated_buckets.profile: Same reason. ax-03 and ax-04 in the Phase 1 batch scored 0.449-0.499 against the master, which cannot be separated from genuine drift without an off-axis positive distribution.

limits: SFace and ArcFace are trained on real photographs; every image here is synthetic and most came from one model family, which can inflate both distributions. The positive set is 20 pairs from 2 characters. Treat the thresholds as an operating point that separates this material, not as a general face-verification result.
